summary.one_liner: Focalboard is an open source, self-hosted project management tool presented as an alternative to Trello, Notion, and Asana, offered as a desktop app or multi-user personal server.
summary.what_it_does: Focalboard helps define, organize, track and manage work for individuals and teams. It ships in two editions: a Personal Desktop app for single-user use on macOS, Windows, or Linux, and a Personal Server that is a standalone multi-user server. The README describes building the server with make commands, running it from bin/focalboard-server, and configuring the port in config.json. It can also package the server into standalone desktop apps that run locally against SQLite, and provides a Docker image (mattermost/focalboard). The README also covers unit testing via make ci, which runs server tests, ESLint, web app unit tests, and Cypress UI tests. The README states the project is multilingual.
use_cases: kanban-style task tracking for a team
Trello or Notion alternative on my own server
running a multi-user boards server in Docker
desktop task board offline with SQLite
how_to_run: Create an .env file in the focalboard directory containing EXCLUDE_ENTERPRISE="1"
stack: Electron-style desktop packaging via make targets (mac-app, win-wpf-app, linux-app)
notable: Two editions: single-user Personal Desktop app and multi-user Personal Server
Desktop apps packaged from the same server running against SQLite
Multilingual, self-hosted, positioned as an alternative to Trello, Notion, and Asana
caveats: README warns the repository is currently not maintained
Only contains standalone Focalboard; the Mattermost plugin lives in a separate repository (mattermost/mattermost-plugin-boards)
Desktop builds are platform-specific; cross-compilation is not fully supported and Windows build needs Windows 10 SDK and .NET 4.8 developer pack
keywords: track work in a self-hosted app
